newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF HINGIS V PIZZICHINI.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF HINGIS V PIZZICHINI.

text.p: Analysis of Thursday's French Open women's singles second round match between world number one Martina Hingis and Gloria Pizzichini of Italy, won 3-6 6-4 6-1 by Hingis.

Hingis made a terrible start, losing the first four games in succession before clawing her way back to 4-3. But the motivated Pizzichini was not to be denied, breaking her opponent for the third time in a set in which Hingis was responsible for 18 unforced errors.

Hingis, playing with a little more composure, went 3-0 up only to experience another apparent total loss of confidence which allowed Pizzichini to storm into a 4-3 lead. Serving for a 5-3 lead, however, she produced a double fault to allow Hingis back to deuce and was made to pay as her Swiss opponent reeled off the next two games as well.

The initiative was now totally with Hingis as she broke her opponent twice with ease to go 5-0 ahead. Pizzichini at least had the consolation of holding serve for 5-1 but Hingis quickly settled the issue after one hour 32 minutes on the Suzanne Lenglen showcourt.
